service.name: Corporate event DJ
service.serviceType: Open-format DJ for corporate events, late-night receptions and private parties
service.description: Open-format DJ for corporate events and private parties across Denver and the Colorado mountain corridor, on its own or carrying the late night after a band through the same sound system on one contract.

faqs.q: Can the DJ follow the band on the same contract?
faqs.a: Yes. Once we are in the building the call-out is already paid, so the DJ added to a band booking bills at the hourly rate only, through the same sound system and on the same invoice. The handoff is planned against your run of show.

faqs.q: What does the DJ booking include?
faqs.a: Decks, booth and a PA sized to the venue, a dedicated announcement microphone on its own channel, load-in and strike, a certificate of insurance naming your venue, a W-9 and one itemised invoice. Sound is inside the published figure at every size, this one included.

faqs.q: How late can the DJ play?
faqs.a: As late as the venue allows. Added time bills at the same hourly rate in 30-minute increments, agreed on the night with whoever holds the budget, and there is no overtime rate. Venue curfews and decibel caps are honoured as written and built into the plan at contract.

faqs.q: What is the DJ plus live instrument option?
faqs.a: A live bass or saxophone played on the floor over the set. It reads as a crowd watching something happen rather than a playlist, and it holds a dance floor late. It is a named option priced on the rate card, quoted as its own line when you ask for it.

faqs.q: Do you take requests on the night?
faqs.a: From you, always, and from guests where they fit. A do-not-play list is the part worth spending time on before the event. A request that would empty the floor gets a straight answer and an alternative rather than a yes and a bad twenty minutes.
